cases.name: Debra Louise Jackson Larned
cases.about:
She worked at a Ramada Inn in Amarillo in 1978 and, later that year, at an assisted living center called Bur-Mont Inc. in Azle, Texas. Police believe she also worked at R.E. West and C.G. Cole Admiral PTR, Realty Investment LTD, in 1979.

https://www.kvue.com/article/news/crime/1979-orange-socks-cold-case-victim-identified-as-debra-jackson-of-abilene/269-376d1bed-b35a-49ab-b3cf-12c73358cb8a
cases.narrative: On 10/31/1979, her body was found in a culvert on Interstate 35. She had been dragged and thrown over a guardrail and was naked except for a pair of orange socks.

cases.name: Lindsey Quinones
cases.about: She was an interior designer and owned her own home staging business.
cases.narrative:
Georgetown Police were alerted to the situation by the 13-year-old daughter. She called 911 just before 3 a.m. and said that her father, Ricardo, entered the home with a weapon and held her and her mother hostage. The child was able to escape the house through a window and into police custody.

Police report that while officers were trying to negotiate with Ricardo Quinones, they heard two gun shots and then entered the home. That’s when officers found Lindsey Quinones deceased.

cases.name: Susan H. Carnes
cases.about: Her obituary said, "Susan taught school for 27 years in Austin, Taylor and Georgetown.  She made life-long friends in fellow teachers and administrators and positively impacted the students who received her instruction.  She was kind, generous, and patient.  She also had a stubborn streak that her family attributed to her Czech and German heritage, and she would do anything for those who were privileged to be loved by her.  She was a tomboy as a girl, an athlete, a cheerleader, a devout Catholic, a teacher, a beloved daughter, a mother, a grandmother, a sister, an aunt, a friend to many."
